profit_quality.assessment: Main denominator uses the three-year median parent net profit of US$34.135m, but cash conversion is weak: 2023 and 2024 operating cash flow were negative, and 2024 profit coincided with large inventory, trade receivable and finance lease receivable expansion. Therefore only 25% is treated as sustainable distributable cash profit.
adjustments: Excluded reliance on bank deposit interest and other investment income as operating cash profit support.
Observed 2024 investment income of US$13.491m and fair value loss on investment properties of US$5.466m as non-operating items.
Used 2022-2024 parent net profit series US$46.340m, US$19.438m and US$34.135m; median US$34.135m.
Applied 0.25 profit haircut because operating cash flow was US$64.406m in 2022, then -US$20.809m in 2023 and -US$61.686m in 2024.
profit_quality.cashflow_support: 2024 operating cash flow was -US$61.686m after US$91.276m inventory increase and US$63.494m trade receivable increases; purchase of PPE was US$9.049m and segment capital expenditure additions were US$58.102m.
profit_quality.haircut_reason: Two consecutive negative operating cash flow years and growth in receivables/inventory/leased container assets show profits are not consistently available as distributable cash.
profit_quality.cash_conversion_assessment: Three-year operating cash flow divided by parent profit: 2022 1.39x, 2023 -1.07x, 2024 -1.81x.
profit_quality.maintenance_capex_assessment: Cash PPE purchases were US$9.049m in 2024; segment capital expenditure additions were US$58.102m, indicating leasing/manufacturing expansion absorbs cash beyond simple maintenance.
profit_quality.working_capital_assessment: 2024 working capital movements absorbed more than US$100m before payables offset; this is the core reason for the low cash-profit haircut.
